To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

quercetin-3- and quercetin 4'-glucopyranoside glycosides, the most abundant flavonoids in onions, have markedly different biological activities compared with the quercetin (3,4'-hydroxyflavone) aglycone.

quercetin-3-4'-diglucose, the major flavonol glycoside in onion bulbs and the flavonol glycone most efficiently absorbed by the human body, is a weak inhibitor of lipid peroxidation and antioxidant activity, but a strong inducer of the phase II detoxifying enzyme quinine reductase.
quercetin-3-4'-diglucose and quercetin 4'-glucopyranose are the most abundant flavonoids in onions, and are preferentially absorbed in humans compared to the flavanone aglycone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and quantification of the flavonoid glycoconjugates in onions, and with the elucidation of the bioactivities of these compounds in comparison with the flavonoid quercetin agylcone.
the bioactivity and absorption of flavonoid glycones from dietary onions.
the identification of dietary components with anticancer activity and the elucidation of the mechanisms involved in this activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bioactivities of dietary flavonoids are not only dependent on the chemical structure of the flavonoid, but also on the nature and the position of sugar substitutions.
the bioactivity of quercetin is highly dependent on its glycosylation pattern.
the glycosylation of flavonoids can dramatically affect their bioactivities, which in turn could affect their biological significance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
quercetin agylcone has the most pronounced bioactivity, but quercetin-3- glucoside and quertecin-4'-glucose are also bioactive, and that quercetin- 3,4'-glucside and rutin are not bioactive.
the 4'-glycoflavones are more potent QR inducers than the 3-glycoflavones and that 4'-glycones are better 'antioxidants' than 3-glycosides.
the quercetin glycone is not as good an antioxidant in vitro as the quercetin 3-glucosides, and is not as good as a QR inducer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glycosylation pattern of flavonoids is a key determinant of bioactivity.
the glycosylation pattern of the quercetin molecule has a profound effect on its biological properties.

quercetin-3-glycosides, such as isoquercitrins, are the major contributors to the antioxidant properties of onions, whereas quercetin- 4'-glucides are the main contributors to the QR-inducing properties of onions.
